clue.text: Make known Imogen is to leave

parts.note: the setter Imogen saying 'I am', shortened to I'M
to part is to go away or leave

explanation.surface: The setter announces that she is quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for 'I', so 'Imogen is' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart news is to pass it on, a direct synonym for revealing or making it known.

clue.text: One is a Muslim leader

parts.note: 'one is' spoken in the first person is I'M, 'I am'
taken as written

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Muslim

explanation.surface: A plain statement that someone is a leader among Muslims.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: I'M + A + the leading letter of Muslim.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads prayers in a mosque, so a Muslim leader in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Feebleness of verse amid superior work, rhymes initially out of place

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other
something out of place has been shifted from where it belongs, so one letter is relocated

parts.note: poetry as a superior form of literary work; 'rhymes initially' points at its R, the letter that moves
V is the standard abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A critic complaining of weak verse in a lofty work whose rhymes are badly placed.
explanation.walkthrough: The R (first letter of rhymes) in POETRY swaps a place to give POERTY, and V then goes in the middle: PO-V-ERTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty can mean deficiency or inadequacy, as in poverty of ideas, so it fits feebleness.

clue.text: One making hasty repair, taking only a second

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: one who 'runs up' a quick repair, to run up being to make something hastily

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the competitor who finishes in second place

explanation.surface: A rushed fix-it job that takes a mere moment.
explanation.walkthrough: To run up a garment is to make it quickly, so one who runs up a repair is a runner-up; 'a second' is not a moment but second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner-up is the contestant who comes second; read literally it is someone who runs something up quickly.

clue.text: Force moving mass to part of gut

indicators.note: moving one thing to another means bringing it up against it, so the pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics
the omentum is a fold of membrane attached to the stomach and intestines

explanation.surface: A physics or medical note about pushing a mass into the intestines.
explanation.walkthrough: The omentum is an anatomical term: a fatty apron of membrane hanging from the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the impetus or driving power of something in motion, a common sense of force.

clue.text: Dreamy prediction of creamy onion soup

indicators.note: soup is a mixture in which ingredients are stirred together and lose their order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe title for a cream-of-onion soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soup' looks like the dish being described; it is the signal to scramble the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneiromancy is divination by interpreting dreams, from Greek oneiros, dream, so a prophecy drawn from dreams.

clue.text: Bent pipes fitted in fuel bowser

indicators.note: the result is fitted inside the following words, sitting in the run of letters across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of fuel and the start of bowser

explanation.surface: Plumbing detail: curved pipes installed in a fuel tanker.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowser is a tanker truck that carries fuel, a mainly British and Australian word.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing an elbow is a curved joint, so a bent section of pipe.

clue.text: Songsters no end shy, internally tense on edges of copse

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so a letter is placed within the word
having no end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: timid is a synonym for shy
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last only

parts.note: the first and last letters of copse

explanation.surface: Birdsong in a wood: timid songbirds, nervous at the fringes of a copse.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMID loses its D to give TIMI; T goes in the middle and the edges of copse follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmice, or tits, are small songbirds, and songster is a literary word for a singing bird.

clue.text: Distance indicator in case somebody takes motorway first

indicators.note: first places the item named just before it at the head of the joined string

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, London to Leeds; the digit 1 reads as I
lest means in case or for fear that
one meaning a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Instructions for a body placed in a case on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A milestone is a roadside stone marking the miles to a place, so it shows distance.

clue.text: A depression around 5 December, mostly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A weather forecast of a low-pressure system around 5 December.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 December' reads as a date, but the 5 is a Roman numeral and 'December, mostly' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent, the season before Christmas, starts in late November or early December and lies largely within December.

clue.text: Prepare me a blunt sedative

indicators.note: to prepare is to make ready by working on something, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient asking to be given a crude sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: Nembutal is a brand name for pentobarbital, a barbiturate drug used to sedate.

clue.text: Little pests come silently: by end of day, crop is flattened

parts.note: to creep is to move quietly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the last letter of day
a crop or craw is the pouch in a bird's throat
something that lies flat is laid out flattened

explanation.surface: Insects sneaking in overnight, leaving the field crop flattened by dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks agricultural but is the bird's crop, the craw.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy-crawlies is an informal name for small insects and spiders, the small pests in a house or garden.

clue.text: Strange mysteries in TV series

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd mysteries turning up in a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but its two letters are needed in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes Minister was a BBC sitcom of the 1980s about a hapless British government minister and his civil servants.

clue.text: My view is available on request

definitions.text: My view is available on request

parts.words: My view is available on request
parts.note: surface reading: an expert offering opinions to anyone who asks; setter's reading: the opinion is introduced by a stock phrase that literally makes it conditional on someone asking

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a set phrase used to introduce one's opinion; read literally it says the opinion is given only if asked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom prefaces a personal opinion, and its literal words make the opinion conditional on a question.

clue.text: Old American, light skinned, holding British to be useless

parts.note: the Incas were the pre-Columbian people of Peru

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: pale-skinned, fair in complexion
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Describing an ancient fair-skinned American who held a Briton captive and proved hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapable means lacking the ability to do things, so ineffective and useless.

clue.text: Love what fallen hero becomes, they say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nil, the score of nothing in tennis

definitions.text: what fallen hero becomes, they say
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the saying 'from hero to' this, of a disgraced celebrity

explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' sounds like a homophone signal, but it points to the idiom 'from hero to zero', not a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring love means nothing, a nought, and the idiom describes a sudden fall from celebrity to nobody.

clue.text: Non-tenured job that's a cushy one, getting in at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the start, so a pair of letters taken from inside is moved up to the head

parts.note: a sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work

explanation.surface: An academic grumbling that the comfortable post went to someone else's insider at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The IN of SINECURE is lifted from second place to the very top, leaving SECURE behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A post without tenure has no guaranteed permanence, so it is insecure, lacking job security.

clue.text: Gently persuade to announce drinks

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: Cokes, colas, said out loud

explanation.surface: Coaxing someone into announcing that the drinks are ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade by soft words and flattery rather than force.

clue.text: Champion, uptight inside, has to get going

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece sits in the middle of another

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: tight gives taut, pulled tight; the up in front of it is the signal to turn it

explanation.surface: A tense champion has to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uptight' looks like one word meaning nervous; it splits into a reversal signal and the word tight.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate is to set a machine or process in motion, a formal word for making something get going.

clue.text: Green annual meeting not disrupted?

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether an environmental party's yearly conference went off undisturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green annual meeting' reads as a political AGM; the definition is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant annual garden plant, and its name also covers a greyish-green shade.

clue.text: Article on tax turning up in restaurant

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up flips the letters so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
re means on or concerning
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a tax showing up on the bill in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: AN + RE + VAT is read upwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant or café.

clue.text: A rook and a rodent revealed when flood receded

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for a rook
'and' joins; 'a' is taken as written
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A bird and a rat seen as floodwaters fall away.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook and the rodent fit the Noah story's animals, but the rook is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Noah's ark comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat as the waters of the Flood go down.

clue.text: Dad's right, each year's a very long time — after the first, go

indicators.note: keeping only what comes after the first letter means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: p.a. abbreviates per annum, each year
an eternity is a seemingly endless time
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A father complaining that his yearly entitlement feels endless to wait for.
explanation.walkthrough: ETERNITY loses its first letter to give TERNITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternity leave is time off work a father is entitled to around a child's birth, so a father's right.

clue.text: Naff way Americans treat colour

definitions.note: a phrase describing how the word is spelt, read as 'no U'
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: American spelling gives colour with no letter U

explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky; U and non-U were 1950s labels for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U describes behaviour or speech marked as not upper class, which overlaps with naff, meaning tasteless or uncool.

clue.text: Left impression, puncturing smart politician

indicators.note: puncturing means piercing into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to smart and to bite both mean to sting
L is the abbreviation for left
an air is an impression or appearance, as in 'an air of calm'

explanation.surface: A left-wing remark that deflated a sharp politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' suggests Labour politics, which suits a follower of Tony Blair, but here it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blairite is a supporter of Tony Blair, the UK Labour prime minister 1997 to 2007, and his politics.

clue.text: Book Suzi? Time to move on

indicators.note: time, abbreviated to its initial, is told to move on, so that letter shifts further along the word

parts.note: Suzi Quatro, the American rock singer and bassist famous in 1970s Britain

explanation.surface: A fan asking if the singer's day is done and it is time to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in QUATRO moves one place further on, past the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size made by folding sheets twice into four leaves, and so a book of that format.

clue.text: They pick the last of the readers

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of the
a lector is a reader, especially one who reads lessons in church

explanation.surface: Choosing the final readers, as for a reading list or a shortlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last of the readers' reads as one phrase, but 'the last of' applies to the word the.
explanation.definitionFit: Electors are voters, people who choose or pick a candidate.

clue.text: Second sight of the French uniform on volcanic island a bit off

indicators.note: with a bit off, a small part is cut from the end of the word
in an across clue one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named piece is placed second

parts.note: de is French for of; it also forms du, des
Java is a volcanic island of Indonesia
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A French clairvoyant in uniform on a volcanic island feeling slightly off.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'uniform on' a word puts U after it; JAVA loses its last letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the feeling of having seen something before, so in effect seeing it a second time.
